title: Reconstruct Itinerary
prompt:
Given a list of airline `tickets` `[from, to]`, reconstruct the itinerary that uses **all** tickets exactly once, starting from `"JFK"`. If multiple valid itineraries exist, return the one with the smallest lexical order.

**Example**: `[["MUC","LHR"],["JFK","MUC"],["SFO","SJC"],["LHR","SFO"]]` → `["JFK","MUC","LHR","SFO","SJC"]`.

This is an Eulerian path — Hierholzer's algorithm, visiting destinations in sorted order.

tests.note: greedy-smallest would strand a ticket; Hierholzer handles it

hints: Build adjacency as a min-heap (or sorted list) of destinations per airport, so you always try the smallest first.
Hierholzer: DFS/iterative — keep going to the smallest unused destination; when stuck, prepend the dead-end airport to the route.
Prepending on the way back builds the Eulerian path in reverse, correctly handling airports you must return through.

solution.explanation: Greedily taking the smallest destination can strand you at a dead end while tickets remain. Hierholzer's algorithm fixes this: when you get stuck, that airport is finalized as the current end of the route (prepended), and you back up to consume remaining edges — assembling the Eulerian path from the tail forward. Min-heaps enforce lexical order.
